investigation_relevance: Directly triggered Michael Kemp MP's drone-expansion petition and this whole investigation. Whether the headline quote itself represents support for drone deployment cannot be established until the full article is obtained (Q-0008).

source_title: "Bring Police Drones to the Mid North Coast" petition text
source_location: Externally hosted Mailchimp petition, linked from a top-level "Drone Petition" item on Michael Kemp MP's official electorate website (exact Mailchimp URL not captured)
evidence_description: Full petition wording, as supplied verbatim by the case operator to the external research pass: the petition asserts the Moree trial "has demonstrated" improved safety with a 50% crime drop, cites 100+ arrests, 70+ stolen vehicles recovered and six missing people located, claims 30-60 second deployment and "a fraction of the cost of a police helicopter", and calls on the NSW Government and Police Minister to expand the remote-drone program to the Mid North Coast and prioritise regional communities. It supplies no source citations, baseline dates, metric definitions, methodology, cost calculation or rollout design of its own.
relevant_quotation: The six-month trial in Moree has demonstrated how drone technology can support frontline police and improve community safety, with initial reports showing a 50% drop in crime.
investigation_relevance: The central public representation this whole case audits. Every numeric claim in it is separately tested in Q-0002 through Q-0004.

source_title: Regional crime inquiry at Kempsey hears from victims
source_location: https://www.abc.net.au/news/2024-10-29/regional-crime-inquiry-at-kempsey-hears-from-victims/104528766
evidence_description: Contemporaneous report of a 29 October 2024 NSW parliamentary regional community-safety inquiry hearing in Kempsey. Records Gail Cheers giving evidence that she and her husband do not sleep at night because of repeated victimisation fears, and recorded emphasis on early intervention, safe accommodation, education, and coordinated work with young people and families - not drone technology.
relevant_quotation: she and her husband do not sleep at night
investigation_relevance: Establishes that the "I don't sleep at night" phrasing used in the 2026 Macleay Argus headline existed in the Kempsey crime record almost two years before the drone petition, attached to a person whose recorded policy emphasis was early intervention rather than surveillance technology.

source_title: Negative-search finding: no controlling RPAS/PolAir-Remote policy in the public policy index
source_location: NSW Police public policy index (exact URL not captured; browsable index at police.nsw.gov.au)
evidence_description: NSW Police previously told Parliament that RPAS use must comply with its CASA Operator Certificate and relevant NSW Police policies and procedures, but the current public policy/procedure index does not expose a policy named for RPAS, PolAir-Remote or facial recognition. This does not establish that no internal policy exists, only that it is not publicly inspectable through the index checked.
investigation_relevance: The operational controls for launch authority, proactive patrol, recording, retention, secondary use, analytics and biometric linkage are not publicly traceable - the central reason GIPA Application 2 exists.

source_title: Negative-search finding: no current facial-recognition use established in the PolAir-Remote workflow
source_location: https://legislation.nsw.gov.au/ (Road Transport Act 2013, s 271A; exact deep-link not captured)
evidence_description: No evidence located establishes that Moree PolAir-Remote currently performs onboard or live facial-recognition identification. NSW does have statutory facial-biometric matching infrastructure available to authorised participating agencies under the National Facial Biometric Matching Capability framework (Road Transport Act 2013 s 271A), but whether PolAir-Remote imagery can be, or has been, submitted to it is unresolved.
investigation_relevance: The correct control question is system linkage (collection -> retention -> face extraction -> external biometric matching), not merely whether facial recognition is embedded in the aircraft itself - see Q-0006.

source_title: Negative-search finding: no evidence PolAir imagery has been submitted for biometric matching
source_location: https://legislation.nsw.gov.au/ (Road Transport Act 2013, s 271A; exact deep-link not captured)

investigation_relevance: Function-creep control is absent from the petition's public case: it does not specify limits on facial recognition, biometric matching, automated person identification or retrospective analytics applied to stored imagery.

source_title: Law Enforcement Conduct Commission Act 2016 (NSW) - complaint jurisdiction
source_location: NSW legislation - Law Enforcement Conduct Commission Act 2016 (exact deep-link not captured)
evidence_description: Section 35 of the Law Enforcement Conduct Commission Act 2016 allows any person to complain about NSW Police Force conduct that is or could be agency maladministration. The Act's objects expressly include identifying systemic issues and assessing the effectiveness and appropriateness of police procedures concerning legality and propriety - LECC can examine systemic practice, not only individual officer misconduct.
investigation_relevance: Establishes a real, currently-available complaint and systemic-review route for PolAir-Remote governance concerns (tasking, discriminatory effect, privacy boundaries, inadequate governance), independent of any individual-officer allegation.

source_authority: LECC / NSW Information and Privacy Commission / NSW Ombudsman / NSW Audit Office
source_title: Negative-search finding: no published PolAir-Remote oversight finding located
source_location: NSW legislation - Law Enforcement Conduct Commission Act 2016 (exact deep-link not captured) | NSW Police InfoLink / GIPA request guidance page (exact URL not captured)
evidence_description: Targeted searches did not locate any PolAir-Remote-specific published investigation, audit or determination from LECC, the NSW Information and Privacy Commission, NSW Ombudsman, or NSW Audit Office. This does not establish that no complaints, internal inquiries or unpublished oversight activity exist.
investigation_relevance: The complaint/access routes exist in principle (EV-0026) but no independent oversight body has yet published anything specific to PolAir-Remote - the practical accountability gap is that a resident who does not know a drone observed their property has no obvious way to discover it and lodge a complaint.

source_title: Headline-phrase provenance finding
source_location: https://www.abc.net.au/news/2024-10-29/regional-crime-inquiry-at-kempsey-hears-from-victims/104528766
evidence_description: The 2026 Macleay Argus headline phrase ("I don't sleep at night") is attributable, in its earlier documented use, to Gail Cheers' 2024 evidence at the Kempsey parliamentary inquiry - not to any newly-identified 2026 drone-specific source. Whether the 2026 article is quoting Cheers again, a new interview, or another person using similar words remains unresolved pending the full article (Q-0008).
investigation_relevance: A victim's fear of crime and endorsement of a particular surveillance technology are separate propositions; until the full 2026 article is obtained, it is unsafe to infer that the headline quotation represents support for the drone proposal.

source_title: Mid North Coast Police District and Oxley electorate geographic scope
source_location: https://www.police.nsw.gov.au/about_us/regions_commands_districts/northern_region/mid_north_coast | NSW Parliament member profile for Michael Peter Kemp MP (exact URL not captured)
evidence_description: The Mid North Coast Police District includes multiple widely-separated stations and communities (West Kempsey, Bellbrook, Gladstone, South West Rocks, Macksville, Nambucca Heads, Port Macquarie, Wauchope, Laurieton, Bowraville, Comboyne and others); Kemp's own Oxley electorate covers 9,325.32 square kilometres. Kempsey Shire itself is geographically dispersed, with existing council CCTV spread across several distinct localities rather than one compact zone.
investigation_relevance: A single Moree-style docked-drone installation has finite operational radius, endurance and communications range - it is not equivalent to coverage of "the Mid North Coast" as the petition's wording requests. The petition does not state the number of docks, aircraft, base locations or response-time standard it is actually asking for.

source_authority: Moree Online News / NSW Police Force
source_title: Continued operational use beyond the stated six-month trial window
source_location: Moree Online News / NSW Police media release, 5 August 2026 (exact URL not captured)
evidence_description: On 8 January 2026, Moree Online News reported the trial would run for six months and "came into effect today". NSW Police-originated material then records PolAir-Remote assisting an arrest arising from a 2 August 2026 incident - nearly seven months after the stated commencement, and reported 5 August 2026. The program was also officially launched a second time on 19 February 2026, creating ambiguity over which date NSW Police treats as the trial's operative clock. No public notice locating an extension, transition period, or revised end date has been found.
investigation_relevance: Establishes the program remained operationally active well past its own publicly stated six-month window, without any located public explanation - continuation beyond the window is verified; any legal or procedural impropriety in that continuation is not established.

source_title: YR-2026-0012 - Aviation Command Operating Model Review (EOI)
source_location: Buy NSW procurement opportunity YR-2026-0012 (exact URL not captured)
evidence_description: On 7 April 2026, five weeks before the RPAS Panel EOI (EV-0013), NSW Police published a separate EOI seeking specialist aviation providers to inform a possible Aviation Command Operating Model Review - covering governance, regulatory compliance, workforce sustainability, training, fleet, engineering, operational efficiency and capacity across the whole of Aviation Command. It expressly states it does not itself procure services.
investigation_relevance: Shows PolAir-Remote/RPAS expansion sits inside a broader command-wide operating-model review, not just the RPAS-specific panel (EV-0013) - the governance and cost architecture a Mid North Coast rollout would actually be decided within is larger than either procurement instrument alone.

source_authority: NSW Government (Buy NSW / eTendering; Have Your Say)
source_title: Enterprise RPAS capability planning preceded the Moree consultation's close
source_location: Buy NSW procurement opportunity YR-2026-0058 | NSW Government Have Your Say - Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems (Moree)
evidence_description: EOI YR-2026-0058 (statewide RPAS Panel) was published 2 June 2026, while the Moree community consultation on the RPAS trial remained open until 12 June 2026 - ten days later. The EOI was non-binding market research, not an award decision.
investigation_relevance: Precise dating showing enterprise-scale capability planning was already underway before the public consultation on the original trial had even closed. Does not establish a predetermined rollout decision - the EOI is described as market research - but does show institutional preparation running in parallel with, not strictly after, public input.

source_title: Statewide scaling was contemplated from the program's inception
source_location: Moree Online News, 8 January 2026 briefing | ABC News, 19 February 2026 formal launch coverage
evidence_description: At the 8 January 2026 trial-commencement briefing, Assistant Commissioner Andrew Holland said that if the trial succeeded it would be spread to other NSW locations and described the project as "the next step in policing". At the 19 February 2026 formal launch, Commissioner Mal Lanyon said the trial would determine whether the program should be scaled up.
investigation_relevance: Establishes that statewide scaling was part of the program's public framing from day one, not a later addition - relevant context for assessing whether the August 2026 Kemp petition is requesting something genuinely still undecided or effectively already contemplated by NSW Police leadership.

source_title: Negative-search finding, reconfirmed: no RPAS panel award established
source_location: Buy NSW procurement opportunity YR-2026-0058 (exact URL not captured)
evidence_description: As at this later check, the Buy NSW opportunity page for EOI YR-2026-0058 still showed no posted notices, and a search of located NSW Police contract-disclosure records did not establish an RPAS panel contract award. An estimated decision date having passed is not itself evidence an award occurred.
investigation_relevance: Reconfirms EV-0014's finding at a later check point - the procurement outcome remains genuinely undisclosed, not merely unchecked.

source_title: Negative-search finding: no public stop, failure, or decommissioning criteria located
source_location: NSW Police public policy index | Buy NSW procurement opportunity YR-2026-0058
evidence_description: No public material located specifies a threshold at which Moree PolAir-Remote would be judged unsuccessful and stopped, nor public criteria for removing docks, ceasing Remote Operations Centre tasking, decommissioning data integrations, or ending operational use. This does not prove such criteria do not exist internally - it establishes they are not publicly auditable in the material located.
investigation_relevance: Combined with continued operational use past the stated six-month window (EV-0037), statewide scaling framing from inception (EV-0040), and parallel enterprise capability planning (EV-0038, EV-0039), this is the clearest evidence gap bearing on whether the program has any working exit path at all, as distinct from whether it should expand further.
